trends.what: A curated list of free public APIs for developers to use in their projects.
trends.why: It's a go-to resource for developers looking to quickly find APIs for prototyping, learning, or building side projects.

trends.what: An open-source platform offering free coding lessons, projects, and certifications in web development, math, and computer science.
trends.why: It remains a top destination for self-taught programmers seeking free, structured, and community-supported education.

trends.what: A massive collection of freely available programming books, tutorials, and learning resources in multiple languages.
trends.why: It's a one-stop shop for free learning materials, especially valuable as education costs rise and developers seek affordable upskilling.

trends.what: A personal AI assistant that runs on any OS and platform, designed to be your always-available digital helper.
trends.why: It's trending because it offers a cross-platform, open-source alternative to proprietary AI assistants, giving users more control and privacy.

trends.what: Interactive roadmaps, guides, and educational content to help developers plan and grow their careers.
trends.why: It's a popular visual and structured way for developers to navigate the overwhelming number of tech skills and career paths.

trends.what: A tool that makes AI agents generate code with the mindset of a lazy senior developer, prioritizing minimal and simple solutions.
trends.why: It's trending because it addresses the common problem of AI over-engineering code, promoting efficiency and maintainability.

trends.what: A fullscreen, mouse-interactive terminal UI (TUI) harness for coding agents, designed for extensibility and developer control.
trends.why: It's gaining attention as a powerful, customizable interface for AI-assisted coding, appealing to developers who prefer terminal-based workflows.

trends.what: A pure C, zero-dependency runtime that runs frontier mixture-of-experts (MoE) AI models on consumer hardware by streaming experts from disk.
trends.why: It's trending because it democratizes access to large AI models, letting people run them on existing hardware without expensive GPUs.
